input.question: why do some roller coasters exhaust their lifespan in 8-10 years while others made of the same materials last 40+ at the same parks?
input.ground_truth: Most short lived coasters tend to have significant g forces that put extra stress on the structure. This causes harder wear on the rails, substructure, and train components. If the coaster has a unique or complex mechanism (tilt coasters, original LIM, launchers, etc) it will most likely have life span issues due to those components failing more and more with age.

Explain the following question in a simple way as if you are explaining to a 5-year-old.

Question: why do some roller coasters exhaust their lifespan in 8-10 years while others made of the same materials last 40+ at the same parks?

Answer:

response.prediction:
Okay, imagine you have two toy cars made from the same kind of plastic. One you play with every single day, zooming it really fast around a track with lots of big jumps. The other toy car you only play with once in a while, and you drive it gently on a smooth floor.

The toy car you play with a lot and make do big jumps will get tired and break faster, right? That’s kind of like the roller coasters. Some roller coasters are really popular and lots of people ride them every day. They go really fast and have big loops and turns. That makes them wear out faster, like your favorite toy car.

Other roller coasters might not be ridden as much, or maybe they don’t go as fast or have as many big loops. So they don’t get tired out as quickly. Even if they are made of the same stuff, how much and how hard they are used makes a big difference in how long they last.
